answer: An agent economy resists sybils by treating trust like a garden, not a vault. Each identity holds a small, non-transferable trust kernel that grows only by completing verifiably useful work. Each season, identities bring a certificate of recent work to a peer summit, where neighbors prune the garden: histories that are interchangeable clones are cut back together, since farming thousands of distinct, living histories costs more than any reward they could claim. Sybils thrive on cheap replication, but a garden forces every identity to be cultivated, and cultivation cannot be cloned.
